title: Regional proxy fastpath vs slowpath synthesis (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft: compare two regional proxy behaviors (fastpath: lightweight TCP/UDP forwarding + minimal buffering; slowpath: full HTTP/1.1 termination with middleware hooks) across a set of synthetic workloads and cost extrapolations. Primary question: when does proxy behavior dominate latency and unit cost, and what knobs give the best cost/latency tradeoff for regional routing?

Test matrix (summary)
- Models: small-chat-7b, chat-13b, embed-lite-1.
- Hardware: gpus-up2 (A100-like), gpus-x1 (H100-like), cpu-edge-8 (x86 multicore).
- Regions: us-east, eu-central, ap-southeast.
- Proxy modes: FASTPATH (L4 pass-through, TLS passthrough), SLOWPATH (L7 terminate, auth + header enrichment + rate limiter).
- QPS targets: 10, 50, 200, 1000 simult requests (sessionized).
- Payloads: short (10 tokens), medium (64 tokens), long (512 tokens).
- Measurement window: 30m steady-state, 10m ramp, 10m cooldown.

Harness notes:
- Client cadence: Poisson arrivals with configurable burst factor.
- KV cache warm before run: 20 minutes of mixed traffic to reach steady hit rates.
- Observability: token-level timing, network raster (RTT), proxy CPU/RAM, kernel context switches.
- Cost inputs: instance hourly list price, estimated GPU amortization, egress per-GB by region.

Raw observations (representative extracts)
1) Fastpath vs slowpath p50/p90/p99 for medium payload (64 tokens) @ 200 QPS, us-east -> eu-central model placement:
   FASTPATH: p50=42ms, p90=78ms, p99=210ms
   SLOWPATH: p50=68ms, p90=135ms, p99=420ms
   delta (p90): +57ms, (p99): +210ms

2) Effect of payload length at 50 QPS, us-east local model on gpus-up2:
   short (10 tok) FASTPATH: p90=26ms | SLOWPATH: p90=48ms
   long (512 tok) FASTPATH: p90=410ms | SLOWPATH: p90=455ms
   note: slowpath overhead is relatively constant (~18-30ms) for short-medium, but for long sequences server-side decode dominates and proxy overhead fraction shrinks.

3) Cost per 1k requests (approx): using blended instance/hr rates and egress assumptions
   - FASTPATH (us-east): $0.96 / 1k (short), $1.60 / 1k (medium), $6.80 / 1k (long)
   - SLOWPATH (us-east): $1.12 / 1k (short), $1.88 / 1k (medium), $7.05 / 1k (long)
   differential driven by extra CPU cycles in proxy + extra tail latency (more headroom needed).

ASCII charts (percentile traces simplified)
- p50/p90/p99 trace across QPS sweep (medium payload)
   QPS   | FASTPATH p90 (ms) | SLOWPATH p90 (ms)
   ------+-------------------+------------------
   10    | 35                | 50
   50    | 48                | 86
   200   | 78                | 135
   1000  | 210               | 480

- p99 amplification factor (p99 / p50) at 200 QPS, medium payload
   FASTPATH: 210/42 = 5.0x
   SLOWPATH: 420/68 = 6.2x

Interpretation / heuristics
- Fastpath gives a consistent latency reduction across short->medium workloads; wins are largest at medium QPS ranges (50-500) where proxy CPU contention + TLS termination in slowpath increases queueing.
- At very high QPS (>=800) both modes hit server-side queueing and GPU IO; proxy adds multiplicative tail effects if middleware blocking operations are present (auth checks, sync logging).
- Long payloads dominated by decode time; proxy optimizations (L4 keepalives, header compression) still help but marginal impact on p99 is small relative to model compute.
- Cost sensitivity: the unit-cost uplift from slowpath is most visible for short requests where proxy CPU is amortized against tiny server compute. For long requests, the relative cost gap narrows.

Operational recommendations (draft)
1) Default regional route: FASTPATH for developer-tier and standard-production routes that do not require heavy L7 middleware.
2) SLOWPATH: reserved for routes that require policy enforcement (fine-grained auth, content scanning) or must attach rich contextual metadata.
3) Adaptive switching: implement a lightweight probe and annotation system that can move specific client IPs to SLOWPATH when policy triggers fire (rate-limited). Avoid global shift on transient spikes.
4) Tail mitigation: for SLOWPATH, convert any blocking auth checks into async tokens where possible (issue short-lived assertion and proceed) and batch outbound telemetry to avoid request-path sync cost.
5) Prefiltering: run small-size signature checks at FASTPATH edge (bypass strict heuristics) to reduce cold transfers to SLOWPATH.

Open questions / next experiments
- How does mutual TLS termination vs passthrough with session resumption change p99 under the same CPU budget? (we only tested TLS passthrough for FASTPATH, TLS terminate on SLOWPATH).
- What is the real-world distribution effect for client mixes where 70% are short requests and 30% are long? Cost model needs a mixed-run sweep.
- Can we quantify the benefit of kernel-bypass frameworks (io_uring style) in the proxy worker compared to optimized NGINX + envoy builds?
- Measure effect of synchronous external auth (okta/idp) vs cached token validation at SLOWPATH.

TODOs
- Run mixed distribution sweep (10/64/512 = 70/25/5) across regions and produce heatmap. (Owner: Ethan)
- Prototype async-auth header pattern in slowpath and measure p99 delta. (Owner: Jonas)
- Cost model: add market-instance discount curves, and per-region egress sensitivity. (Owner: Marisol)

Quick notes for product collateral
- Two-sentence summary for docs page: "Regional proxy choice affects user-visible latency and unit economics. For throughput-focused LLM serving, use FASTPATH to reduce p90 tails and lower unit cost; reserve SLOWPATH for routes that require heavy policy or enrichment."
- Chart to include: p90 vs QPS curve (FASTPATH vs SLOWPATH) and cost per 1k requests by payload size.

Appendix: small example of request timing breakdown (medium payload, 200 QPS)
- client-to-proxy RTT: 12ms (median), proxy internal queue: FASTPATH med=3ms, slowpath med=25ms (includes header processing, auth lookup cached hit), network transit + model latencies: 27ms p50, model decode tail adds variable amount up to +180ms at p99.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally compact and rough. Data slices and full CSVs are in the linked artifacts (bench repo). We should standardize nomenclature: use FASTPATH/SLOWPATH rather than L4/L7 in user-facing collateral.
- If we want to craft a single-page one-pager for sales, we should include a risk band: short-high-QPS customers (chat bots, autocompletion) see the largest unit-cost benefit from FASTPATH.

End of draft.
